Hi Maya — thanks for the note and the clear ask. Happy to help.

In short: we have a published IO ratecard for hosted that splits input/output per 1M tokens and a model catalog that shows per-model performance profiles. I’ve attached our standard ratecard PDF to this thread and summarized the baseline below.

Baseline (public hosted):
- Standard models (e.g., Redwood-Base, Redwood-Chat): $20 / 1M tokens input, $80 / 1M tokens output (combined billing: input + output)
- Large/LLM-optimized families (long-context variants, high-throughput configs): +20% on top of baseline
- Embeddings: $15 / 1M embedding tokens (separate product SKU)

Notes:
- The attached PDF is our standard public ratecard and includes the model roster and per-model notes (latency tiers, recommended contexts).
- For pilots in the 500k–2M tokens/mo range we typically offer a pilot discount or credits depending on contract and timelines — happy to align once we know target usage and timelines.

I’m looping in Ben (solutions engineering) to call out any model recommendations for clinical triage use-cases and to offer a short demo if helpful.

Hi Maya — copied from Laura. Quick, concrete answers below plus attached ratecard.

Public hosted baseline (per-1M tokens):
- Input tokens: $18 / 1M
- Output tokens: $72 / 1M
- Combined billing: each request is billed for input + output. Example: 100 input tokens + 900 output tokens = billed as (100/1e6)*$18 + (900/1e6)*$72.

Model roster and pricing nuances:
- Redwood-Base (default low-cost): baseline pricing above. Good for short responses and high throughput.
- Redwood-Chat (conversational family): baseline pricing above; recommended for chat flows with instruction tuning.
- Redwood-Long (extended context): baseline + 20% due to memory/throughput characteristics.
- Redwood-Quant (int8 quantized variants): baseline - 10% for latency-tolerant workloads but best-effort quality.

Pilot credit / discount guidance:
- For a 3-month POC at 500k–2M tokens/mo we can provide either:
  - $5k in platform credits applied to hosted usage, or
  - a 15% invoice credit if you commit to a short-term paid pilot and share a public case study (mutually agreed).

Compliance note: hosted API is SOC2-compliant; for PHI we recommend planning for a Dedicated or Private deployment later in the lifecycle, but de-identified prompts are fine for an exploratory POC. If you’d like, Ben can run a quick perf/quality sweep on a representative prompt set.

Attachment: Redwood_Standard_Ratecard_v1.pdf

—Aditya
